facts.text: A JSONL data file name must match dossier-NNNN.jsonl with at least four digits, per the JsonlDataFileRegex pattern.
An asset path written into a bundle must be assets/ plus 64 lowercase hex characters and an optional extension.
Every JSONL line escapes U+2028, U+2029 and U+0085 because those characters split lines in several readers.
Each line is encoded as UTF-8 without a BOM and ends with one appended newline byte.
StricterLimit keeps the smaller of the flag and profile values, and uses the non-zero one when the other is zero.
Every limit error message is built through Fail, which appends the words nothing was written.
Without a MemoryCeilingBytes setting, the in-memory ceiling falls back to Array.MaxLength.
A subject record carries parent only when the parent subject is itself part of the same bundle.
A subject pin is written only when it is an object whose repo and rev members are both strings.
With the assets mode set to none, publish writes no asset records and no asset files.
Attachments are deduplicated by sha256, so a blob shared by two facts is emitted only once.
A blob absent from the store produces a warning and an asset record marked missing, and publish continues.
Embedding an asset larger than MaxEmbedAssetBytes raises asset_too_large_to_embed.
Profile extension checking always includes jsonl, then adds each asset file's extension.
A profile that forbids an extension the bundle needs raises profile_extension_not_allowed.
Data files are packed greedily in record order, and a record is never split across files.
A single record larger than the file limit raises record_exceeds_max_file_bytes instead of being split.
max_files_exceeded fires when data files plus asset files exceed the limit, with manifest.json not counted.
max_total_bytes_exceeded compares the total bytes of data and asset files against the limit.
An embedded asset line is refused when its base64 length plus one newline byte exceeds the file limit.
A data file whose packed bytes exceed the in-memory ceiling raises bundle_too_large_for_memory.
Each data file is named dossier-NNNN.jsonl from a D4 padded counter rendered in the invariant culture.
The bundle hash hashes each file name and its sha256, then each asset path and its sha256, in sorted order.
Each file_stats entry records bytes, lines and sha256 for one emitted data file.
The manifest files list holds the data files, the asset paths and manifest.json, sorted ordinally.
The manifest is indented and written with newline separators rather than the platform default.
An asset file whose size exceeds the file limit also raises record_exceeds_max_file_bytes.
PublishJsonl exports subjects and live facts only; superseded, retracted and dossier-kind facts are left out.
The previous manifest's file list is passed to WriteBundle, which removes the files it names.
A subject record always writes an aliases array, even when the subject carries no aliases.
An embedded asset record carries a data field and an encoding field set to base64.
Import rejects a blank From directory with invalid_from before it opens any store connection.
A From path that is not an existing directory raises bundle_not_found.
A manifest format other than markdown or JsonlFormatId raises unsupported_bundle_format.
The markdown reader enumerates every .md file below the bundle root and keeps those matching FactPathRegex.
A markdown bundle with no fact files raises bundle_has_no_facts, whose message names the --facts detail requirement.
A markdown fact file whose machine record cannot be parsed is skipped and recorded, not fatal.
Two fact files claiming the same fact id raise import_duplicate_id, naming both paths.
When no fact file yields a readable machine record, import raises bundle_has_no_records.
Markdown fact files are ordered ordinally by their bundle-relative path before parsing.
Two live facts claiming the same subject, kind and key raise import_slot_conflict before any row is inserted.
Only records that carry a key and whose status is neither superseded nor retracted take part in the slot check.
A subject id already present in the store raises import_subject_exists, whose message asks for an empty database.
A fact id already present in the store raises import_fact_exists.
Facts are inserted ordered by posted_at, then by bundle order, then by path.
The content hash is recomputed on import from text, data and the ref inputs instead of being read from the bundle.
The facts_fts row joins the fact tags with single spaces for its tags column.
The live slot is pointed at the fact only for keyed records that are neither superseded nor retracted.
Refs are inserted with a seq counter that starts at zero and follows record order.
Attachment rows are written with INSERT OR REPLACE, keyed on fact id and sha256.
Blobs are counted once per distinct sha256, even when several attachments share the same bytes.
PruneChanges runs inside the import transaction immediately before the commit.
Subject, fact, ref and attachment rows all commit in one transaction, so a failure leaves the store untouched.
Items are round-tripped through ItemInput so a republish prints them identically.
PostedAt returns the provenance posted_at string, or null when provenance is not an object.
An attachment whose blob cannot be restored is recorded as a skip naming the attachment sha256 and the reason.
Subjects are inserted in ordinal order of their id, inside the same transaction that inserts the facts.
A ref whose valid field is missing is stored as null, while true and false become one and zero.
ImportResult counts one attachment per row written, while blobs counts only distinct sha256 values.
The slot check walks every record before the connection is opened, so a conflict touches no database.
at: var slots = new Dictionary<(string Subject, string Kind, string Key), ImportRecord>();

facts.text: RestoreBlob refuses a sha256 that is not 64 lowercase hex characters and returns a skip reason instead.
at: sha256 is not 64 lowercase hex characters

facts.text: The blob source path is the record's subject directory plus assets/ and the attachment's asset file name.
When the bytes are absent, the store keeps the attachment row without its blob and reports a skip.
at: the store keeps the attachment row without its blob

facts.text: Bytes that do not hash to the recorded sha256 are not restored and are reported as a skip.
An existing blob file under BlobRoot is left untouched rather than rewritten.
The blob directory is created only when a blob is about to be written.
A manifest subject entry defaults its name to the map key and its kind to subject when they are omitted.
A subject known only from a fact record gets kind subject, no parent, no aliases and no pin.
A manifest that cannot be parsed as JSON is ignored; only the subjects the fact records name are then used.
at: An unreadable manifest only costs the subject metadata

facts.text: A manifest pin is kept only when it is a JSON object, and it is stored as canonical JSON.
ParseImportRecord searches for the last Machine record heading before splitting the remainder into lines.
A file with no Machine record section is skipped with a message saying the bundle predates machine records.
A machine record section that holds no lines is skipped with the message machine record section is empty.
A machine record section whose first line is not a json code fence is skipped.
at: machine record has no json code fence

facts.text: A json fence that is never closed ends the record with the message machine record code fence is not closed.
at: machine record code fence is not closed

facts.text: A machine record whose JSON root is not an object is skipped.
at: machine record is not a json object

facts.text: Invalid JSON in a machine record is skipped, and the parser message is appended to the skip reason.
at: machine record is not valid json:

facts.text: A record missing id, subject_id, kind, status or a string text is skipped with that reason.
at: machine record lacks id, subject_id, kind, status or text

facts.text: A confidence that is missing or not a number defaults to 1.0.
A record with no provenance field gets an empty JSON object instead.
